rationale: Deflating accruals by market cap is a well-worn variant of the accrual anomaly (accruals-to-price / percent-accrual robustness checks) rather than a genuine interaction, and the 1/ME scaling means the cross-sectional dispersion is dominated by a size/value tilt in the magnitude of the ratio rather than by any accrual–value complementarity.

The product of two demeaned z-scores is large and positive both when the firm is cheap with conservative accruals and when it is expensive with aggressive accruals, so the long leg pools the hypothesized best stocks with the theoretically worst ones — the expression does not compute the stated complementarity, and the claimed orthogonality to main effects holds only under symmetry assumptions that raw z-scores of skewed accounting ratios will violate.

GROWTH(B/M) over one year is dominated by the denominator, so the "value news" leg is essentially the negative of past 12-month return, making this largely a repackaged loser/reversal bet whose positive expected sign sits awkwardly against annual momentum, and the paper's economic story about de-rating without accounting deterioration is not what the price-driven leg actually isolates.

A cash-converted EBITDA yield on an enterprise-value anchor is a coherent and genuinely distinct construction from the archive's equity-anchored attempts, though the unwinsorized EV denominator can approach zero or turn negative for net-cash firms and will need trimming to avoid outlier-driven results.

This is structurally the same rank-difference template as the archived AccrualRegimeReversalValue/OpaqueOtherAccrualValue with dividend yield — itself a long-published anomaly — swapped in for B/M, and the large mass of zero-dividend firms creates exactly the rank mass point the sibling proposals were designed to avoid.

It reuses the archived ConjunctiveValueAccrualScreen's MIN aggregation while swapping in two textbook published anomalies (earnings yield and Hafzalla-style percent accruals), so it reads as a deflator variant of an already-tested signal, and the |ib| denominator explodes for near-zero-earnings firms without any winsorization.
